attributes.residual: NONE - EXACT. fndiff --clean MATCH (0 real diff lines, pool-name noise only), --ops opcode streams identical 65/65, regnorm 71 paired / 0 renaming / 0 STRUCTURAL / 0 unpaired -> EXACT, slotdiff SLOT MAP IDENTICAL. THREE INDEPENDENT FIXES, in the order they were found. (1) THE SLOT: the declared first parameter was f64 maxDist. The 16-byte parameter save area (f64 8 + f32* 4 + s32 4) sets the local block FLOOR at 24; the target's floor is 20, which requires a 12-byte parameter area, i.e. an f32 first parameter. Changing f64->f32 moved the volatile f32 root scratch 24->20 and took slotdiff to SLOT MAP IDENTICAL (real 16->12). The GC asm cannot distinguish the two widths at the compare (fcmpo cr0,f6,f1 with an f32 already exact in an FPR), so the FRAME is the only evidence that fixes the signature - this is the whole point of measuring slots rather than reading opcodes. (2) THE ACCUMULATOR: the target's `fmadds f0,f7,f7,f0` then `fmadds f6,f2,f2,f0` keeps the dx*dx+dy*dy intermediate in a scratch and writes d2 exactly once. Two forms that assign d2 once via a plain statement (a parenthesised single expression, and an explicit f32 temp) BOTH emitted an extra fmr at +0x84 - two identical A/Bs, axis dead. The assignment-in-condition form `if ((d2 = dz*dz + (dx*dx + dy*dy)) > 0.0f)` closed it with no fmr (real 12->8). (3) THE LOAD COLOURING: the last 8 lines were the scratch FPRs for the dy/dx worldmat loads. Swapping the SOURCE order of the dx and dy delta statements to dx-first closed them (real 8->0) even though the target EMITS the dy load first - the scheduler reorders, so source order is not readable off emission order.
